observations.statement: The document is a reference inventory governed by DRY, SSOT contract, naming, no-open-question, and deterministic-default constraints; Plans define target behavior while implementation may change.

The window assigns shared-primitive ownership to Crosswalk, storage/projection/persistence/retention ownership to storage-plan, Assistant Chat behavior ownership to assistant-chat-design, and media capability wording ownership to the media owner document.

Debug Mode is a thread-scoped, assistant-led workflow distinct from DAP; its tools are shared across four consumer contexts, its visible evidence is keyed by canonical investigation and instrumentation identities, its six instrumentation states are named, its default sequence is automated, and its remote MVP scope is constrained.

The node graph is the canonical orchestration model; Feature Seam and Work Package are first-class graph-owned objects; blocked identity, requested/effective runtime identity, and route/open primitives are cross-cutting contracts.

Assistant Chat consumes shared runtime identity and route/open primitives, while annotation/review safety details are delegated to detailed contracts and the native in-app review grammar is preferred over browser mediation.

The Orchestrator has a fixed tab-first composition, Progress alone is widget-composed, Source Control is narrow and worktree-first, Seams supersedes Tiers vocabulary, and routing/open primitives are shared rather than GUI-local.
Package Overseer and Seam Overseer are governance roles; subagent and fresh worker are the default node-worker and retry policies; graph patching creates a new generation while retaining lineage.
Usage, recovery, and analytics are runtime-native and use shared runtime identity, blocked-episode identity, and persistent account-pressure/switch history rather than tier-first correlation.
Runtime/storage summaries are attempt-scoped, separate immutable plan structure from mutable runtime projections, and classify tier-era vocabulary as compatibility history.

Scheduler summaries require deterministic scored-ready-set dispatch with attempt, lane, safe-point, remediation, conflict, retry, blocked-outcome, and runtime-event-stream lineage rather than lexical node-id dispatch.
Account switching preserves both latest-state and append-only event records so usage views can reconstruct history rather than display only the newest account label.
Git/worktree operational truth is split between Orchestrator and Source Control, and historical lane identity must survive cleanup of the live worktree.

Rendering keeps source canonical, makes SVG canonical and PNG derived for Mermaid export, guarantees detached preview/browser windows cross-platform, treats embedded webviews as optional, separates trust tiers, and falls back from structured preview edits to source editing.
Source Control, GitHub Actions, and Docker Manager are first-class panels with enumerated subviews; Worktrees remains Source Control's primary object view and lane-first behavior is secondary.

Run detail/history exposes to-repo pivots, panel state is persisted per project where applicable, lineage joins survive restarts, partial chains remain visible with unresolved labels, and blocked/requested-effective behavior remains product-wide.

The scheduler addendum names scored scheduling, pass identity, immutable per-dispatch attempts, distinct attention_required and blocked states, safe-point recovery, remediation-child lineage with shared retry/backoff policy, and pre-lock versus post-lock fallback behavior.

Feature summaries defer web, skill, planning, permission, and approval details to owner docs while naming the web family, slash-command surface, Agent Config/Settings ownership split, connection profile identity, and the Feature Seam help alias boundary.

The feature list owns summary/reference wording while linked ContractRefs own detailed behavior; FL-002 codifies generic traceability acceptance, two validators, no WorkNode compilation, and the same owner boundary.
FL-003 is an accepted structural inventory PlanUnit whose acceptance bars WorkNode creation and whose compile hint names the inventory-section mode.
FL-004 is an accepted owner-deferral PlanUnit whose canonical text, negative constraint, stale disposition, and owner-boundary note all preserve the media capability wording boundary.

candidate_findings.title: MVP scope retains an inclusion-or-deferral fork
candidate_findings.statement: The inventory leaves multi-repository Source Control as “multi-repo source control (or explicit deferral)” even though the document declares no open questions and deterministic defaults; the window states neither the default disposition nor the authority or evidence that selects deferral.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders and acceptance reviewers can reach incompatible MVP scopes while each remains consistent with the same feature summary.

candidate_findings.title: Deterministic scheduler behavior lacks a total decision contract
candidate_findings.statement: The scheduler is required to be deterministic and event-driven, but the window does not state score inputs, a total tie-break order, duplicate-wakeup or idempotency handling, concurrent-pass serialization, or cancellation behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Different implementations can dispatch different attempts or duplicate work under the same ready set and wakeup history, breaking reproducibility and lineage.

candidate_findings.title: Debug lifecycle has states without transition and recovery semantics
candidate_findings.statement: Six instrumentation states and a fully automated sequence are enumerated, but no allowed transition graph, transition triggers, cancellation path, cleanup_failed retry or escalation authority, or idempotency rule is stated in the window.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can disagree on when instrumentation becomes active, when cleanup is terminal, and how leaked or failed cleanup is surfaced and recovered.

candidate_findings.title: Per-project panel and lineage persistence is conditional without defaults
candidate_findings.statement: Panel state is persisted only “where applicable,” while lineage configuration names detail level, category visibility, retain-after-cleanup settings, disabled fallback, and tradeoffs without defining applicability, defaults, data shape, restore or merge behavior, reset behavior, or persistence failure handling.
candidate_findings.impact: Project reopening, migration, cleanup, and disabled-mode behavior can differ across panels and platforms, undermining the promised restart-safe lineage.

candidate_findings.title: Lane-first Source Control behavior leaves a consequential GUI choice open
candidate_findings.statement: The feature permits lane-first to be “an overlay or filter” when lane or package ownership is “known” without defining the known-ownership predicate or selecting the interaction and routing model.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can produce incompatible list semantics, selection state, deep links, and empty or unknown-ownership behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Preview trust and edit validation boundaries are unnamed contracts
candidate_findings.statement: The rendering summary names separate trust tiers and validated structured commands but does not define the trust-tier capability matrix, command schema and validator, rejection behavior, audit evidence, or atomicity and fallback behavior for invalid or partially applied edits.
candidate_findings.impact: Security-sensitive HTML and generated-preview behavior, plus edit integrity, remain implementation-dependent at a boundary the summary explicitly treats as trusted versus restricted.

candidate_findings.title: Artifacts panel contract relies on an unenumerated type count
candidate_findings.statement: The artifact summary asserts 19 runtime artifact types and names cost_usage and Show in Ledger or Usage, but it does not enumerate stable identifiers, schemas, producer and consumer ownership, validation, retention, or route/open behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Artifact producers, storage, filtering, and GUI pivots cannot share a verifiable compatibility contract from this summary, and the stated count has no window-local acceptance oracle.

candidate_findings.title: FL-004 acceptance does not state a semantic media-wording oracle
candidate_findings.statement: FL-004 is accepted and carries a concrete media wording obligation, but its stated acceptance criteria are generic traceability and no-work-node checks and its validation surfaces are named only as migration and index validators; no window-local oracle is stated that rejects an incorrect Gemini mode or account matrix or stale shorthand.
candidate_findings.impact: A structurally valid PlanUnit can be accepted even if the feature summary drifts on the specific capability distinction FL-004 exists to preserve.

candidate_findings.title: FL-002's machine-readable negative constraints are empty
candidate_findings.statement: FL-002 preserves no-open-question and naming constraints and explicitly prohibits WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, and production build tasks, yet its negative_constraints field is empty.
candidate_findings.impact: Consumers that rely on structured negative constraints can miss prohibitions that remain present only in prose, weakening lossless compilation and automated governance.

candidate_findings.title: Node Graph surface naming is not explicitly normalized
candidate_findings.statement: The fixed tab list names Node Graph while the shell-summary sentence names Node Graph Display as the graph-patch lineage surface, without an alias or route-target statement tying the two labels together.
candidate_findings.impact: Tab labels, commands, automation selectors, and documentation can diverge on whether these names identify one surface or two.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Media capability summary ownership and the required Gemini Direct versus Gemini CLI wording are explicit, and stale mixed-account or bare key-exception shorthand is explicitly rejected.
Debug Mode is explicitly distinct from the classical DAP surface, evidence ingress is visible and identity-linked, and arbitrary remote attach plus silent local fallback are explicitly excluded.
The Orchestrator tab set, Progress-only widget composition, Tiers retirement, and shared route/open primitive names are explicit.
Default worker and retry policies and graph-generation lineage behavior are explicit.
Attempt-scoped runtime state, immutable-plan versus mutable-runtime separation, scored-ready-set dispatch, and the historical status of tier-era or lexical dispatch vocabulary are explicit.
Account switching explicitly requires both current-state fields and append-only events sufficient to reconstruct switch history.

The rendering summary explicitly keeps source canonical, identifies SVG as canonical and PNG as derived, guarantees detached windows cross-platform, makes embedded webviews optional, and defines source-edit fallback.
Run-to-repo lineage explicitly survives cleanup and restarts, and incomplete joins remain visible with unresolved labels instead of being hidden or overclaimed.

The scheduler summary explicitly distinguishes attention_required from blocked, safe-point recovery from restore points, remediation children from parent attempts, and pre-lock fallback from post-lock integrity stop.

The PlanUnit acceptance text explicitly preserves source spans and owner references, forbids executable work-node artifacts, names validation surfaces, and disables WorkNode creation in the compile hint.
The owner/consumer boundary explicitly limits feature-list ownership to preserved summary behavior and follows ContractRefs for cross-document ownership.

unknowns.statement: The concrete schemas, type constraints, validation rules, and versioning behavior for shared blocked identity, requested/effective runtime identity, and route/open primitives cannot be determined from this window.

Exact prompt-determinism, provider-variance, precedence/conflict, thread-isolation, recovery, audit-event, and privacy behavior for annotation and selection-to-chat review is unknown here because the summary assigns it to detailed contracts.

No accessibility behavior is stated for the enumerated Orchestrator, Source Control, GitHub Actions, Docker Manager, preview, or detached-window surfaces, so keyboard, focus, screen-reader, scaling, and reduced-motion obligations cannot be established from the window.
The definition and validation of a PM-managed remote-mode project, and the user-visible failure and evidence behavior for a rejected remote target, are not stated.

Web-tool inputs, outputs, error and retry semantics, batch ordering, cancellation replacement behavior, and deprecated /cancel alias behavior cannot be determined from the summary; it expressly defers refined behavior to owner sections.
The document says Part 2 records current codebase behavior, but Part 2 is outside this assigned core; no current implementation state can be verified from the window.
The referenced FL-002 source-lineage record was not inspectable under the blind scope, so the claimed lossless span mapping and its receipt cannot be independently verified.

Context establishes that FL-005 begins and repeats the Debug Mode summary, but the remainder of that PlanUnit is outside the assigned ranges, so its dependencies, acceptance criteria, validation surfaces, and structured constraints cannot be assessed.
Whether the detailed owner documents resolve any candidate gaps identified in this reference summary is unknown because those documents were outside the permitted blind scope.

This document exists to avoid losing features when writing rewrite implementation docs. Part 1 lists planned and new features from the Plans folder, organized by category and relation. Part 2 records what exists in the codebase today for reference. Plans define target behavior; implementation may change.
- **Crosswalk** — `Plans/Crosswalk.md`; ownership boundaries for shared primitives and cross-surface responsibilities.
- **storage-plan** — `Plans/storage-plan.md`; canonical storage, projection, persistence, and artifact-retention semantics.
- **assistant-chat-design** — `Plans/assistant-chat-design.md`; canonical Assistant Chat behavior, modes, thread UX, and slash-command semantics.

- **Media generation and capabilities** — `Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md`; canonical for capability discovery and media generation routing. Feature summaries MUST defer Gemini media/account capability wording to the owner docs: Gemini Direct is key-only/API-key-backed, Gemini CLI is mode-dependent across OAuth/API-key/Google-credential rows, and stale-canon `mixed-account` or bare `key-exception` shorthand is not a complete feature description.

Debug Mode is the rewrite-era assistant investigation workflow: it treats diagnosis, instrumentation, evidence capture, verification, and cleanup as one coherent thread-scoped operation rather than as disconnected debugger gestures. The feature matters because Puppet Master must support automated, evidence-first debugging without collapsing Debug Mode into classical DAP debugger semantics or into opaque agent-only behavior.

- Assistant Chat exposes `Debug` as a first-class assistant-led primary mode distinct from the classical `Debugger`, `DAP Debugger`, and `/DAP` surface
- Debug-capable tools remain shared platform capabilities across Assistant, Orchestrator, Interview, and delegated runs
- investigations use canonical `investigation_id`, `instrumentation_id`, visible Investigation Context, and runtime-artifact linkage rather than hidden evidence ingress
- instrumentation lifecycle states are explicit: `planned`, `active`, `collecting`, `cleanup_pending`, `cleaned`, and `cleanup_failed`
- default Debug behavior is fully automated, evidence-first reproduction / diagnosis / fix / verification / cleanup under a run-scoped Debug Automation Profile
- remote Debug MVP applies to local projects and PM-managed remote-mode projects only; no arbitrary ad-hoc remote attach and no silent local fallback

- node graph is the canonical orchestration model
- `Feature Seam` and `Work Package` are first-class graph-owned objects
- runtime blocked identity, requested/effective runtime identity, and route/open primitives are canonical cross-cutting contracts

- assistant chat consumes shared requested/effective runtime identity rather than defining local schema
- chat navigation, usage pivots, and source-open behavior align to `route_target`, `OpenSubject`, and `OpenFile`
- document annotation and selection-to-chat review is a cross-surface feature with runtime `/safety` boundaries: prompt determinism, provider variance handling, audit/event clarity, precedence/conflict handling, thread isolation, resume/recovery, and sensitivity/privacy boundaries remain owned by the detailed contracts rather than by this feature index
- external `open-plan-annotator` research is background only: it demonstrated a browser-based local review UI opened from a hook/plugin flow, with deletion/comment/insertion/replacement actions, approve vs deny/request changes, and structured markdown feedback, but Puppet Master keeps the stronger review grammar in native in-app document/chat surfaces instead of browser mediation

- Orchestrator remains tab-first with `Progress`, `Plan Compile`, `Seams`, `Node Graph`, `Evidence`, `History`, and `Ledger`
- `Progress` is the only widget-composed Orchestrator tab
- Source Control remains narrow and worktree-first
- Orchestrator shell summaries are tab-first rather than widget-first: `Progress` is widget-hosting, `Plan Compile` is the plans-to-code projection tab, `Seams` is the `/package-oriented` replacement for stale `Tiers` language, `Node Graph Display` is preserved as the graph-patch lineage surface, and `Evidence`, `History`, and `Ledger` remain peer tabs rather than hidden composite-reference details.
- `Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md` may still explain widget-based Tiers as historical scaffolding, but feature copy treats `Tiers` as `/superseded` display vocabulary and keeps `Seams` plus package-oriented ownership as the live object model.
- Crosswalk-level summaries must name routing/open primitives directly: `route_target`, `OpenSubject`, `/open-by-identity`, FileManager `open-by-identity`, runtime-artifact envelopes, and artifact-opening behavior are shared cross-surface contracts rather than local GUI conveniences.

- `Package Overseer` and `Seam Overseer` are governance roles
- default node worker policy is `subagent`
- default retry policy is `fresh worker`
- graph patching creates new graph generations while preserving historical lineage

Usage, recovery, and analytics are modeled as runtime-native records rather than as optional UI summaries. The rewrite uses shared runtime identity, blocked-episode lineage, and persistent account history so usage analysis and recovery flows can explain what happened, who acted, and why the system transitioned between states.

- usage correlation is runtime-first, not `tier_id`-first
- blocked approvals and recovery use runtime blocked-episode identity
- account pressure and account-switch history are first-class shared runtime records

Feature summaries must describe the runtime/storage/schema backbone as attempt-scoped execution state, not as mutable plan-shard state. `Plans/storage-plan.md`, `Plans/usage-feature.md`, `Plans/plan_graph.schema.json`, `Plans/project_plan_node.schema.json`, `/plan_graph.schema.json`, `/project_plan_node.schema.json`, `/storage-plan.md`, and `/usage-feature.md` remain the detailed owners; this reference keeps only the feature-level consequences. The legacy `/phase/iteration`, `tier_runtime_record`, and `tier_id` vocabulary is compatibility history, while live behavior uses `attempt_id`, `scheduler_lane`, safe-point recovery, blocked lineage, package/seam/lane promotion, and the `/storage/schema` separation between immutable plan structure and mutable runtime projections. The `/seam/lane/promotion` summary is a feature alias for package completion, seam transition, lane/worktree identity, and promotion records owned by the runtime contracts.

Scheduler and recovery summaries must preserve deterministic scored ready-set behavior rather than drifting back to lexicographic `node_id` dispatch. Feature copy may name `node_id` for correlation, but dispatch is based on the scored ready-set, `attempt_id`, `scheduler_lane`, first-class safe-point metadata, remediation child lineage, `worktree-conflict` handling, graph-local retry lineage, blocked/runtime outcomes, and the `/runtime/storage` event stream. Any `tier-era` or lexical-dispatch phrasing is explicitly historical and must not own the current scheduler contract.

Account-switching summaries preserve both latest-state and append-only event requirements. Runtime identity features include `account.switched`, `recent_switch_reason`, `account_switch_reason`, effective/requested account fields, and account-pressure history as first-class `/runtime` records, so usage views can reconstruct the switch-history rather than reading only the newest account label.

The Git/worktree feature family separates orchestration truth from concrete repository operations so that historical execution lineage survives even when a live worktree is cleaned up or re-bound. This prevents Source Control actions from erasing the audit trail that Orchestrator, Assistant Chat, and recovery flows rely on.

- lane/worktree lifecycle is split between Orchestrator operational truth and Source Control concrete Git actions
- historical lane identity survives live worktree cleanup

This addendum captures the rewrite's document and preview rendering model: source remains canonical, rendered output is first-class, and richer preview experiences never replace the underlying editable artifact. The same rendering pipeline must support chat, planning docs, editor preview, and future deeper planning surfaces without introducing a hidden document model.

- Mermaid export as SVG (canonical) and PNG (derived).
- Full Markdown support centered on source-canonical editing plus rendered preview, not on replacing Markdown with a hidden WYSIWYG model.
- HTML files support both source editing and full rendered browser-like viewing.
- Built-in browser, rendered preview, and click-to-context are separate from web/read tool lineage: `web_search`, `web_fetch`, `read-website`, and `/site-reader` remain discovery or Site Reader/read-path concepts and must not own the visible editor-tab/detached browser product surface.
- Image files render natively in the Slint app surface.
- Detached preview/browser windows are first-class, cross-platform guaranteed behavior.
- Embedded webviews are optional optimizations, not required product invariants.
- Generated Markdown/Mermaid previews use a restricted trust tier; full HTML/browser mode uses a separate trust tier.
- Preview-mode edits are limited to validated structured commands and otherwise fall back to source editing.

- first-class `Source Control` side-panel surface with Changes, History, Graph, Worktrees, and Branches / Stash
- first-class `GitHub Actions` side-panel surface with Current Branch, Workflows, and Settings
- first-class `Docker Manager` side-panel surface with Containers, Images, Compose, Registries, Build / Bake, Publish / Unraid, and project-focused Kubernetes
- external `/current` reference research validates these as parity-plus feature families, not speculative extras: Source Control carries `/history/stash/merge-editor/worktree` expectations, GitHub Actions readiness is split into name/scope-based sub-capabilities, and Docker/Kubernetes scope is project-focused rather than cluster-administration.
- Source Control keeps `Worktrees` as the primary subview and `/object` list; lane-first is an overlay or filter when lane/package ownership is known, not the replacement object model.

- `Run-to-repo lineage` remains a GUI cross-surface differentiator, not optional polish: Orchestrator run detail and history rows show `to-repo` pivots into Source Control, GitHub Actions, and Docker Manager `destination-panel` views so users can trace which worktree, branch, commits, PR, Actions runs, publish artifacts, `/deploy` outputs, and Operation receipts came from a given run or `/attempt`.

- Source Control, GitHub Actions, and Docker Manager panel state persisted per project where applicable
- Run-to-repo lineage state includes lineage detail level, derived artifact category visibility, and retain-after-cleanup `/settings`; `/event/storage` receipt joins preserve SCM, Actions, publish, and Kubernetes identifiers across restarts, while partial chains remain visible with unresolved labels instead of hiding known lineage. `/disabled` fallback and `/tradeoffs` are explicit: lineage must survive cleanup and restarts without overclaiming incomplete joins.
- new canonical command families for Source Control, GitHub Actions, Docker Manager, and cross-surface pivots
- blocked-state and requested-vs-effective rules remain product-wide behavior, not panel-local polish

- deterministic scored ready-set scheduling instead of pure lexical dispatch
- event-driven queue-analysis passes keyed by `scheduler_pass_id`
- immutable attempt lineage with new `attempt_id` per dispatch and explicit runtime fields for retry/blocking/remediation/safe points
- blocked outcomes with explicit recovery actions instead of generic failures, with distinct `attention_required` vs `blocked` wizard/thread/dashboard states
- safe-point-backed recovery distinct from user-facing restore points
- remediation child execution with explicit lineage and shared failure-class retry/backoff policy
- pre-lock-only draft decomposition fallback and post-lock graph-integrity stop behavior

unit_type: requirement
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/feature-list.md
canonical_text: >-
  Debug Mode is the rewrite-era assistant investigation workflow spanning diagnosis, instrumentation, evidence capture, verification, and cleanup with canonical investigation and instrumentation identity, shared debug-capable tooling, automated evidence-first behavior, and constrained remote Debug MVP scope.
